stem: Which one of the following angles is an obtuse angle?
solution: An obtuse angle is bigger than $90^\circ$ and smaller than $180^\circ$.
Test the options against these two limits: $90^\circ$ is exactly a right angle and $180^\circ$ is exactly a straight angle, so neither of them is obtuse.
${=a}^\circ$ is smaller than $90^\circ$, so it is an acute angle, and ${=r}^\circ$ is bigger than $180^\circ$, so it is a reflex angle.
Only ${=o}^\circ$ lies between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$, so it is the obtuse angle.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Counts a right angle as obtuse
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student takes 'obtuse' to start at $90^\circ$ instead of just above it, so an angle of exactly $90^\circ$ is called obtuse (the open lower limit of the obtuse range is missed).

notes: Reverses the book's direction: the book gives an angle and asks for its type (ex 7.8 no. 1b, 1f); here the type is given and the student picks the size. The stem never changes, so distinct_by_choices is set; the options carry the variation (o, a, r are drawn independently, thousands of distinct option sets). Each option is a different type: obtuse (correct, 91 to 179 so near-boundary values such as 91 and 179 occur), straight 180, right 90, acute a, reflex r. The two 'wide angle' distractors (180 and a reflex) share the catalogued id obtuse-for-any-wide-angle; the acute option carries swaps-acute-and-obtuse. The 90 option carries a newly proposed id. Exactly one option can be obtuse by construction (bands are disjoint).
